question: Which of the following Nuclear Power Plant is situated in the state of Uttar Pradesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Narora Atomic Power Station** (NAPS) is located in Narora, in the Bulandshahar district of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• NAPS is operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).
 
• The plant has two reactors, each with a capacity of 220 MW, making a total capacity of 440 MW.
 
• It uses Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR) technology, which uses heavy water (D2O) as both moderator and coolant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thumba**

 
 
• Thumba is known for the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS), which is located in Kerala, not a nuclear power plant.
 
 
 
• **Tarapur**
 
 
• Tarapur Atomic Power Station (TAPS) is located in Maharashtra and is the oldest atomic power station in India.
 
 
 
• **Rawatbhata**
 
 
• Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station (RAPS) is located in Rajasthan and has a series of PHWR reactors.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL)**
 
 
• NPCIL is a government-owned corporation responsible for the generation of nuclear power for electricity.
 
• It operates under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), Government of India.
 
• NPCIL was created in September 1987 under the Companies Act 1956, with the objective of operating atomic power stations and implementing atomic power projects for electricity generation.
 
 
 
• **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR)**
 
 
• PHWR is a type of nuclear reactor that uses heavy water (deuterium oxide D2O) as its neutron moderator and coolant.
 
• This type of reactor is capable of using natural uranium as fuel, which is an advantage in terms of resource availability.
 
• India has developed expertise in PHWR technology and has several PHWR-based nuclear power plants.
